jobs.description: Employer: Bread Financial Expires: 11/24/2026 Every career journey is personal. That's why we empower you with the tools and support to create your own success story.Be challenged. Be heard. Be valued. Be you ... be here. Job SummaryThe Summer Internship Program at Bread Financial allows college students to develop a variety of skills within different areas of our business. Over the summer, interns will collaborate with several teams and departments, building a firm knowledge of our business and company culture. Participants will also go through a professional curriculum, attend social and philanthropic events, and participate in executive round tables. The program targets rising junior and senior undergraduate students and graduate students.The Operational Excellence organization delivers to the enterprise by engaging all associates in continuous improvement, including simplification, automation, emerging technologies, improved controls, and process redesign. The Analytical and Automation Solutions team within Operational Excellence assesses ideas that call for automation or artificial intelligence (AI), then builds solutions using automation, generative AI and process re-engineering to remove unnecessary steps and make our processes more efficient. As an intern, you will work on real projects alongside a mentor and team members, such as finding automation opportunities, building reports and dashboards, and documenting solutions. This role offers hands-on experience in a dynamic, innovative environment and the chance to present your work at the end of the summer. jobs.title: McLarty Fellow, Africa Practice (DC) at Ankura
jobs.description: Employer: Ankura Expires: 11/24/2026 Ankura is a team of excellence founded on innovation and growth. McLarty Associates, an Ankura Company, is the global strategy firm led by former Clinton White House Chief of Staff Thomas F. “Mack” McLarty, III, former Deputy Secretary of State John D. Negroponte, and President Lee Feinstein. Since 1998, MA has built a team of nearly 100 seasoned international specialists to help corporate and non-profit clients manage policy and government issues around the world. With offices in Washington, Beijing, and Brussels, our people can be found in over twenty countries. In 2022, McLarty Associates joined Ankura Consulting, an independent global expert services and advisory firm. The Ankura-McLarty combination delivers comprehensive solutions to handle disputes, navigate distress, manage risk, address financial and operational challenges, and execute programs that resolve policy, regulatory, government, and diplomatic issues that companies face anywhere in the world. Position Summary:McLarty Associates is seeking a bright, resourceful individual for a paid, entry-level internship/graduate fellowship to support our Africa Practice. We are seeking an individual who can work part-time (approx. 30 hours/week) starting in January 2027. This position will be performed in-person from McLarty’s Washington D.C. office.As an intern/graduate fellow, you will work on a variety of projects with different engagement teams. The program aims to give you exposure to the breadth of our services and client work. You will work closely with our professionals – Associate through Senior Managing Director – and gain first-hand experience in consulting. Your assignments may involve work in news tracking, policy analysis, memo writing, and/or note-taking at client meetings.Essential Duties and Responsibilities:Conducting extensive research of public policy, international, and business issues;Writing memos, compiling biographies, preparing presentations;Monitoring regional news outlets;Attending and reporting on speeches, panel discussions, and policy forums of interest to the firm and clients;Assisting professional staff with general office and administrative support; andOther duties as assigned. Qualifications:We are seeking individuals who are:Graduates of a Bachelor’s or Master’s program in International Relations, Political Science, or related field.Accomplished qualitative and quantitative researchers;Excellent writers;Exceptionally organized with an independent and creative nature;Strong critical thinkers;Inclined to take initiative and anticipate the needs of the team;Attentive to details;Able to operate in a fast-paced work environment while maintaining a high level of professionalism and confidentiality;Able to remain poised under pressure and juggle multiple projects at a time;Proficient with PowerPoint, Excel, Office 365, and other business applications and media platforms. Candidates must be legally authorized to work in the US.Ideal candidates for this position possess an understanding of international politics, economics, trade, technology, government relations, business, culture, and entrepreneurship. Applicants should also have a robust background, demonstrated interest, and/or experience living or studying in sub-Saharan Africa. Regional language proficiency strongly preferred, especially French, or Portuguese. Interested applicants must submit an application that includes: Cover Letter highlighting relevant experience and skills;Resume; andShort Writing Sample (no more than 3 pages) demonstrating strong research and concise writing on issues related to sub-Saharan Africa, international politics, or political economy. Please compile all application materials into one PDF document. We will be accepting applications on a rolling basis. Applying early is strongly encouraged. Ankura is required to include a reasonable estimate of the compensation range for this role. A reasonable estimate of the current payrate for this internship is: $18.40/hr. This position is not benefits eligible. Ankura is an Affirmative Action and Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, or protected veteran status and will not be discriminated against based on disability. Equal Employment Opportunity Posters, if you have a disability and believe you need a reasonable accommodation to search for a job opening, submit an online application, or participate in an interview/assessment, please email accommodations@ankura.com or call toll-free +1.312-583-2122. This email and phone number are created exclusively to assist disabled job seekers whose disability prevents them from being able to apply online. Only messages left for this purpose will be returned. Messages left for other purposes, such as following up on an application or technical issues unrelated to a disability, will not receive a response.

jobs.title: Supplier Quality Engineering Co-op at Alliance Laundry Systems, LLC
jobs.description: Employer: Alliance Laundry Systems, LLC Expires: 11/24/2026 Join Our Team as a Supplier Quality Engineering Co-op! Timing/Duration of Internship/Co-op: Spring/Summer 2027 Co-Op (January to August) or, Summer/Fall 2027 Co-Op (May to December))Ripon, WI — on-site, 1st shift. Most of what goes into a finished product is made by someone else. Do you want to learn how a company makes sure those parts are right — and what happens when they are not? Join our Supplier Quality team in Ripon, WI, as a Supplier Quality Engineering Co-op. Working alongside our Supplier Quality Engineers, you will help qualify new parts, support investigations into supplier issues, and see how a supply base is managed. Why Join Us? Broad Exposure: Support part qualification, supplier audits, and corrective action work across multiple commodities. Real-World Impact: Contribute to qualifications and investigations that continue after your term ends. Professional Development: Learn PPAP, APQP, supplier auditing, and root cause investigation from engineers who do it every day. Supplier quality runs on timelines that do not fit in a summer. A co-op term is long enough to follow those cycles from start to close. Apply now. Your Role: Support the qualification of assigned parts or a commodity group, including helping prepare and review PPAP submissions. Help track open supplier quality issues and assist the team in following them through to resolution. Assist with investigations into non-conforming material, supporting root cause analysis and the documentation of Supplier Corrective Action Requests (SCARs). Participate in supplier audits and technical reviews alongside your mentor, observing how quality systems and process capability are evaluated. Help compile supplier KPIs such as defects per million and on-time delivery, and prepare reject and warranty summaries for the management team. Support APQP activities and assist Design and Manufacturing Engineering with clarifying component specifications and tolerances. What We're Looking For: Skills and Abilities: Problem-solving ability paired with diplomacy and professionalism when communicating with supplier contacts. Blueprint reading ability, or readiness to learn it quickly, including the ability to interpret standards such as ASTM. Functional understanding of statistics as applied to quality, or coursework underway. Strong computer skills, including Excel; familiarity with SAP, Minitab, or Power BI is a plus. Willingness to ask questions and seek direction from your mentor and the broader Quality team. Education: Currently pursuing an associate or bachelor's degree in Engineering, Quality, Manufacturing, or Supply Chain, with sophomore standing or above, and eligible for a multi-term co-op through your school. Physical Requirements: The role involves a mix of sitting for extended periods, standing and walking the production floor, stooping, bending, and minimal lifting. Manual dexterity is also required. Occasional day or overnight travel to domestic supplier sites may be part of this role, always accompanied by your mentor. International travel is not required. Ready to see how the supply base really works? Apply now to join our Supplier Quality team!

jobs.description: Employer: Alliance Laundry Systems, LLC Expires: 11/24/2026 Supplier Quality Engineering Intern Location: Ripon, WI Timing: Summer 2027 Internship Overview We are seeking a curious and detail-oriented Supplier Quality Engineering Intern to support our Quality team in Ripon, Wisconsin. This internship provides exposure to supplier quality management, part qualification, supplier performance data, and the cross-functional collaboration between Quality, Purchasing, and Engineering. The Supplier Quality Engineering Intern will assist with a defined summer project scoped by a mentor, support day-to-day supplier quality activities, and contribute to work that improves how we evaluate and manage our supply base. What You'll Do Support a defined summer project assigned by your mentor, such as helping build a supplier performance scorecard, assisting with a PPAP submission package, or documenting a root cause investigation on a recurring non-conformance. Help analyze supplier performance data — defects per million, on-time delivery, reject and warranty trends — in Excel and SAP, and assist in preparing summaries for the management team. Sit in on supplier audits and technical reviews, virtual and on-site at regional suppliers, and observe how a supplier's quality management system is evaluated. Learn how a Supplier Corrective Action Request (SCAR) is written, issued, and closed, and help maintain the supporting documentation. Observe the APQP process and how launch readiness is assessed before a new part is approved. Help compare supplier process capability data against print requirements and flag gaps for the team to review. Read technical drawings and material standards such as ASTM, and learn what a specification is really asking for. Share your project findings and observations with the Quality and Sourcing teams at the end of the term. What You'll Bring Currently pursuing an associate or bachelor's degree in Engineering, Quality, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, or a related field, with sophomore standing or above. Strong organizational skills and attention to detail. Effective written and verbal communication skills, including professionalism when communicating with contacts outside the company. Ability to gather information, ask thoughtful questions, and work through unfamiliar processes. Comfortable using Microsoft Office tools, particularly Excel; familiarity with SAP, Power BI, Minitab, or SharePoint is a plus. Ability to follow direction while collaborating effectively with teammates across functions and locations. Interest in manufacturing, quality, supply chain, sourcing, or supplier development. Key Competencies Acquires Information: Gathers data from multiple sources, consults with others, and asks effective questions to support assigned work. Communicates Effectively: Clearly and concisely shares information while tailoring communication to the needs of the audience. Supports Coworkers: Responds positively to requests, contributes to team goals, and considers the impact of their work on others. What You'll Gain Hands-on exposure to how a part goes from a drawing to an approved, qualified, shipping component. Experience supporting PPAP, APQP, supplier auditing, and SCAR/CAPA processes. Understanding of what a quality management system audit looks for and why ISO and IATF certification matter. Opportunities to develop data analysis, professional communication, and teamwork skills. A dedicated engineering mentor, regular check-ins, and access to the full Quality team. Physical Requirements and Travel The role involves a mix of sitting for extended periods, standing and walking the production floor, stooping, bending, and minimal lifting. Manual dexterity is also required. Occasional day travel to regional supplier sites may be available as a learning opportunity, always accompanied by your mentor. No overnight or international travel is required.

jobs.description: Employer: Procter & Gamble (P&G) Expires: 11/26/2026 Research and Development (R&D) at Procter & Gamble, the largest consumer packaged goods company in the world, includes a diverse group of roles that contribute to the innovation and development of our products. It encompasses roles in product research, formulation, testing, and scientific analysis. You will find variety and excitement starting Day 1. This internship is specifically designed for individuals working towards a PhD who are developing proficiency in their field. As an intern or co-op in management, you will have the opportunity to learn from experienced professionals in a supportive environment. This is a 12-week paid internship, designed to provide you with a solid foundation for future career growth. The internship will take place from May (potentially early June) to August of 2027. Join us at P&G, where your contributions will play a vital role in shaping the future of consumer products! The Opportunity:P&G has an opportunity for a PhD intern to work in our Corporate R&D to develop an AI-agent-driven framework that automates and accelerates machine learning experimentation for time-series data modeling. The intern will explore how AI agents can propose and execute experiments, modify configurations or code, analyze results, and recommend next steps. This work will investigate improvements in data preprocessing, model architecture, training strategies, and hyperparameter selection while comparing AI-driven research with conventional experimentation in terms of model performance, reproducibility, and research efficiency.The ideal candidate will demonstrate a strong eagerness to learn and grow professionally and possess excellent communication skills—both written and verbal. This role is perfect for those with passion for innovation and problem-solving, along with a proactive attitude and the ability to adapt to new challenges. Join us in this dynamic environment, where your contributions will make a real impact as part of a collaborative team! Key Responsibilities:Review existing literature and techniques in LLM-based AI agents, automated machine learning, and AI-enabled research systems.Prepare time-series datasets and establish a reliable, reproducible baseline model and evaluation pipeline.Design and implement an AI-agent-driven framework for proposing, executing, and analyzing machine learning experiments.Explore improvements in data preprocessing, feature representation, model architecture, training strategies, and hyperparameter selection.Implement appropriate validation, experiment-tracking, and reproducibility practices for AI-generated configurations or code.Compare AI-enabled and conventional experimentation approaches based on model performance, reproducibility, experiment throughput, and research efficiency.Document the framework, experiments, results, limitations, and recommendations.Share key insights and present final results to the broader R&D team. Job QualificationsRequired Qualifications: Education: Working towards a PhD in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Data Science, Electrical Engineering, Statistics, or a related field.Experience developing and evaluating machine learning or deep learning models.Hands-on experience with a deep learning framework such as PyTorch or TensorFlow.Proficiency in Python.Understanding of model training, validation, performance evaluation, and experimental design.Ability to review technical literature, formulate research hypotheses, and translate ideas into reproducible experiments.Available to work a 12-week internship from May/early June to August in the summer of 2027. Available to work 5 days a week in office at Mason, OH location. Preferred Qualifications: Experience with large language models, generative AI, and the design of multi-step agentic workflows or multi-agent systems.Experience with agentic frameworks such as LangGraph and AI observability platforms such as Arize.Experience with automated machine learning, hyperparameter optimization, experiment orchestration, or experiment-tracking systems.Experience in time-series data modeling.A record of research contributions through grants, fellowships, patents, peer-reviewed publications, conference presentations, or relevant open-source projects. If selected for both championships, travel from Toledo to Monterey will be covered by the USGA.What you bring:Undergrad students preferredAble to lift heavy items while practicing Safe Lifting and/or with the assistance of othersAbility to be on your feet for extended periods of time (12+ hours)Strong organizational, planning, communication, and presentation skillsAbility to take initiative and effectively execute directionsCollaborative, high energy, and spiritedCreative thinker and problem-solverInterest in hospitality sales and or serviceThis internship will provide hands-on experience in the exciting world of sports hospitality while contributing to the success of the USGA’s championship hospitality and experiences. jobs.title: Case Resolution Specialist, Employee and Labor Relations | USC at JOB BOARD - Straus Institute and Graduate Law Programs
jobs.description: Employer: JOB BOARD - Straus Institute and Graduate Law Programs Expires: 11/26/2026 The Case Resolution Specialist (CRS) provides impartial consultation, conflict resolution, investigation, and problem solving in response to informal and formal complaints from various campus stakeholders. The CRS conducts inquiries, analysis, and case resolution; assists in the development/maintenance of relevant policies, training, procedures, and guidelines. The CRS is responsible for maintaining accurate, updated records and documentation in case management system. The CRS stays current with modern case resolution methods/best practices to resolve workplace concerns in a proactive manner.Hear from the Employee and Labor Relations teamListen to Valyncia Raphael-Woodward share more about the ELR team, the Case Resolution Specialist role, what makes the work meaningful, and what candidates can expect.Listen to the Role Overview → https://tinyurl.com/caseresolutionspecialist(opens in new window)The work schedule for this opportunity is hybrid, requiring three days onsite a week at our offices in Downtown Los Angeles.Job ResponsibilitiesThe candidate for the position of Case Resolution Specialist will:Conduct impartial, confidential trauma-informed interviews and fact-finding meetings to investigate formal and informal complaints and inquiries. Interview employees, collects appropriate documentation, reviews information from a variety of sources, and provides support as the case is facilitated to resolution, ensuring a well-documented and prompt process for all parties.Document and maintains employee and labor relations and workplace concerns in a case management system in a timely manner. Ensure all employee relations and workplace concerns are addressed.Develop and communicates results, corrective actions, and recommendations for appropriate resolutions to an array of complex workplace issues using a variety of tools (e.g., facilitated dialogue, shuttle diplomacy, other alternative dispute resolution methods). Draft, implement, and monitor informal resolution agreements.Provide outreach and training on matters related to resolving workplace concerns according to university policies, procedures, and processes to various audiences. May work in collaboration with other unit members to perform projects and conduct background research to assist with cases, training, and development of outreach and other programming materials.Assist with writing and maintaining employee policies and procedures, ensuring compliance with university policies and procedures. Work to foster and maintain effective and collegial relationships with internal and external stakeholders in support of the university's goals and values. Stay current with modern case resolution methods and best practices to resolve workplace concerns in a proactive manner. Encourage a workplace culture where all employees are valued, value others and have the opportunity to contribute through their ideas, words and actions, in accordance with the USC Integrity and Accountability Code.Advise leadership on performance management, corrective action, and disciplinary processes with utmost discretion. Provide guidance on rights and responsibilities of management and employee terms and conditions of employment. Interpret policies, employment laws, and labor agreements while guiding consistent and compliant practices that mitigate risk.Consult on, develops and communicates results, corrective actions, and recommendations for appropriate resolutions/resultant actions to an array of complex employee and labor relations issues using a variety of tools (e.g., intake meetings, interviews, facilitated dialogue, shuttle diplomacy, other alternative dispute resolution methods). Draft, implement, and monitor formal and informal resolution plans and. Ensures complete, timely, and accurate documentation in case systems. Maintains knowledge of relationships, labor and employee laws, policies, employment and labor legal trends, and new legislation that could impact the employee/employer relationship.Design and deliver outreach and training to a variety of audiences on matters related to preventing and resolving workplace concerns, managing change, and increasing leader and team effectiveness in alignment with university values policies, procedures. May work in collaboration with other unit members and University Offices to perform projects and conduct background research to assist with cases, training, and development of outreach and other programming materials.Minimum QualificationsThe candidate for the position of Case Resolution Specialist must meet the following qualifications:Bachelor’s Degree from an accredited institution in a related field including but not limited to: business, psychology, communications, employment law, industrial relations or another related fieldFive years of relevant work experience resolving workplace disputes, engaging in conflict resolution in a large, multi-faceted organization, conducting workplace investigations, and/or any equivalent combination of education and experience. Ability to gather, organize, and synthesize information, conduct analysis, document progress, and make effective recommendations for complex and sensitive issues.Sound judgment, high integrity, and problem-solving skills. Knowledge of current major employment laws and regulations (e.g., ADA, FMLA, NLRA). Experience establishing collaborative initiatives with multiple departments. Strong facilitation skills, with a proven track record of building strong collaborative relationships with stakeholders at all levels of an organization. Demonstrated ability to effectively manage time, prioritize tasks and work independently.Ability to gather, organize, and synthesize information, conduct analysis, document progress, and make recommendations for complex and sensitive issues.Ability to adhere and enforce complaint procedures and fundamental components of fair process standards.Knowledge of best practices used to investigate and resolve employee concerns or grievances including best practices as they relate to reducing bias during grievance resolution processes.Proven skill, sensitivity, and experience interacting with a variety of constituents and fostering a culture of belonging and engagement.Demonstrated written and oral communication skills; skill-building rapport in an open, friendly, and accepting way.Ability to present complex issues in a clear, concise, and visually appealing manner.Ability to communicate in writing and verbally for variety of audiences and levels of leadership to inspire further action.Excellent customer service skills.Ability to interpret and apply collective bargaining agreements (CBAs) and labor relations guidance, including NLRB and California PERB requirements.Preferred QualificationsThe ideal candidate for the position of Case Resolution Specialist has the following qualifications:Master’s degree in human resources, psychology, communications, law, industrial relations or another related field, or Juris Doctorate degree.Seven years’ of experience.Experience with iSight, Salesforce, CaseIQ, or other similar case management software or databases.Experience working with a variety of populations in a higher education institutional setting.Experience in, and awareness of, the sensitivity required when interacting with a community on trauma-related topics.Certification and/or experience with complex workplace investigations.Conflict resolution, alternative dispute resolution, or conflict management skills.Strong presentation and facilitation skills with an emphasis on education and training for a variety of constituencies.Demonstrated excellence in writing comprehensive investigative reports.Please submit the following with your application:ResuméCover LetterWriting Sample (will be requested): Candidates selected to move forward in the recruitment process will be required to submit a writing sample. Candidates may provide either a de-identified closure notice from a previous matter or a written response to the provided prompt.The writing sample should be 1–2 pages, no more than 1,200 words, and formatted in 12-point font. Submissions may be redacted or fictionalized as needed to preserve confidentiality.The annual base salary range for this position is $101,000 - $108,000. When extending an offer of employment, the University of Southern California considers factors such as (but not limited to) the scope and responsibilities of the position, the candidate’s work experience, education/training, key skills, internal peer equity, federal, state, and local laws, contractual stipulations, grant funding, as well as external market and organizational considerations.The University of Southern California is an Equal Opportunity EmployerMinimum Education: Bachelor's degree. Additional Education Requirements Combined experience/education as substitute for minimum education Minimum Experience: 5 years 4 years resolving workplace disputes, engaging in conflict resolution in a large, multi-faceted organization, conducting workplace investigations Minimum Skills: Ability to gather, organize, and synthesize information, conduct analysis, document progress, and make recommendations for complex and sensitive issues. Ability to adhere and enforce complaint procedures and fundamental components of fair process standards. Knowledge of best practices used to investigate and resolve employee concerns or grievances including best practices as they relate to reducing bias during grievance resolution processes. Proven skill, sensitivity, and experience interacting with a variety of constituents and fostering a culture of belonging and engagement. Ability to communicate in writing and verbally for variety of audiences and levels of leadership to inspire further action. Excellent customer service skills. Preferred Education: Master's degree In Human Resources Or Psychology Or Communication Or Law Or in related field(s) Or Juris Doctor (JD) Preferred Experience: 7 years Preferred Skills: Experience with iSight case management software or other, similar case management software or database. We design and develop labeling and functional materials, radio-frequency identification (RFID) inlays and tags, software applications that connect the physical and digital, and offerings that enhance branded packaging and carry or display information that improves the customer experience. Serving industries worldwide — including home and personal care, apparel, general retail, e-commerce, logistics, food and grocery, pharmaceuticals and automotive — we employ approximately 35,000 employees in more than 50 countries. From compact residential applications to large commercial projects, Allied Aire Enterprises redefines ease-of-business through breadth of product, resources and competencies unparalleled in the market. At Allied Air Enterprises, we're proof of how effective good people can be. We've based our entire business on hiring talented, dedicated professionals and giving them the resources needed to thrive. You can expect to participate in impactful, developmental projects designed for your specific area of focus. This role will provide you with real work experiences to grow your career and provide exposure to business leaders throughout the company. Successful interns will have the potential opportunity of joining Lennox Full-Time upon graduation. Relocation and/or travel may be required for your position. Why You’ll #LoveLennox:Impactful Projects: Work on meaningful assignments that drive real business results. Your ideas matter here.Intern Community: Connect with peers through social events, team-building activities, and engagement programs.Innovation Exposure: Dive into cutting-edge tech and trends shaping the HVAC and manufacturing industries.Learning and Development: Access workshops, training sessions, and resources to level up your skills and expand your knowledge.Competitive Pay and Relocation Support: Receive a competitive compensation package and relocation support if needed. This rate is based on the intern's current year in their respective university programs. Graduate students may receive a higher rate of pay based on their year in school. Employees in this role are also eligible to earn overtime when they work more than 40 hours in a week (or as otherwise required by state law). Our Culture: At Lennox, our Core Values of Integrity, Respect & Excellence are ingrained in the fabric of the organization. They define our culture – which is about how we do business and how we treat others. Lennox is not just a workplace; we are a global community that values each team member’s contributions. As an equal opportunity employer, we are committed to recruit, develop, and retain talented individuals from a wide range of backgrounds, ensuring that everyone has the opportunity to succeed and contribute to our continued growth and success. At Lennox, you’ll take pride in our brands, knowing you are part of something special. Come, stay, and grow with us!

jobs.title: Winter Internship at National Sports Center for the Disabled
jobs.description: Employer: National Sports Center for the Disabled Expires: 11/27/2026 About the NSCD The National Sports Center for the Disabled (NSCD) is Colorado’s most comprehensive provider of adaptive outdoor experiences. We offer more programs, in more places, in more ways that change lives. As a national leader in adaptive recreation, we empower individuals with disabilities, their caregivers, and communities to rethink ability. Through adaptive innovation, outdoor recreation, and the beauty of Colorado, we transform lives, families, and communities. Our programs help participants rediscover confidence, experience the joy of play, and find motivation to try new things, connect with others, and believe in themselves. With top-tier adaptive equipment, expert coaches, and unmatched mountain and metro programs, we help athletes of all levels push limits and shift perceptions—both their own and the world’s. #RethinkAbility. Position Summary: Winter interns gain hands-on experience with NSCD programs and procedures, assisting in the delivery of adaptive Alpine and Nordic ski lessons. Training and responsibilities align with NCTRC guidelines where applicable. The internship runs from early January to mid-April, with a minimum 14-week commitment at 32–45 hours per week, including weekends and holidays. Most programming takes place at Winter Park Resort, with additional opportunities in Grand County and the Denver Metro area. Housing is provided with at $300 monthly stipend Internship Duties: Intern responsibilities are carried out independently, under supervision, or in coordination with staff. Additional duties may be assigned. • Complete an intern project, case study, and Inservice aligned with educational goals and approved by the intern supervisor.• Support the coordination and delivery of programs. •Assist with registration, customer service, and volunteer training.• Attend required NSCD continuing education sessions.• Contribute to NSCD special events and fundraising efforts.• Drive company vehicles, including trailers and oversized vehicles, as needed. •Follow all safety procedures and use appropriate equipment.• Assist with various activities such as alpine skiing, Nordic skiing, snowboarding, ski bike, sit ski, etc. •Engage daily with participants of all ages and a range of physical, mental, and behavioral disabilities.• Perform other duties as assigned Professional Performance: • Follow all NSCD personnel policies and procedures • Maintain professionalism in performance, appearance, and behavior—serving as a role model on and off duty • Approach work with creativity, teamwork, and a problem-solving mindset • Complete tasks with accuracy, timeliness, and in compliance with agency standards and schedules • Support and promote the agency’s mission of positive individual and social change • Exercise sound judgment and discretion in caring for participants • Demonstrate honesty and integrity in all agency-related matters • Pursue ongoing professional development and training • Foster a culturally sensitive, respectful environment that values diversity and inclusion Other duties may be assigned Education and Experience Required: • Pursuing a degree in Therapeutic Recreation, Adaptive Recreation, Education, Exercise Science, OT/ PT, Social Work, or related field. • Intermediate alpine skiing ability (minimum level 6); must ski and load lifts independently. • Experience working or volunteering in service roles or with individuals with disabilities preferred. • One-on-one experience with people with disabilities. • Able to follow directions and work independently.• Valid driver’s license and ability to pass NSCD background check for driving. Physical Requirements: • Able to work outdoors at high altitude in varying weather and terrain conditions.• Physically capable of assisting with adaptive equipment, transfers, and positioning.• Able to lift at least 75 lbs. with assistance.• Sufficient dexterity, hearing, and vision to operate computers, phones, and interact with participants.• Able to manage multiple high-priority tasks in fast-paced, noisy environments.• Valid U.S. driver’s license and eligible to drive company vehicles, including 16-passenger vans, snowmobiles, and lifts.

(MNA) and Moore Global Network Limited, an independent and global accountancy and business advisory network of CPA and financial services firms located throughout the United States and around the globe. jobs.description: Employer: Moss & Associates Construction Expires: 11/28/2026 Location: Energy Jobsites Across the United StatesEligibility: Students graduating within the next two years About the RoleIf you are a safety-minded student who wants to do more than sit in a classroom — this is your opportunity.Moss & Associates is looking for Energy Safety Interns to join our teams on real, active utility-scale Energy projects across the U.S. This is not a "coffee and spreadsheets" internship. What We're Looking ForRequired:Currently pursuing a degree in one of the fields listed above.Graduating within the next two yearsOpen to relocating for your project assignment.Strong communicator who collaborates well with a teamComfortable using Microsoft Office (Excel, Word, Outlook)Genuinely excited about safety, construction, or renewable energyBonus Points If You Have:Previous experience in construction, preconstruction, or a related internshipFamiliarity with OSHA standards or safety regulations What You'll Get Out of ThisWe know internships are a two-way street — here is what Moss brings to the table:Competitive hourly pay — your time and effort are valued.Housing allowance — available if you are not local to the project site.Real mentorship — direct coaching from experienced project safety leaders, not just busy managersMeaningful work — contribute to large-scale renewable energy projects that matter.A culture you will love — Moss is built on safety, teamwork, and innovation.Resume-worthy experience — walk away with field experience that sets you apart! jobs.feedName: David Nazarian College of Business & Economics
jobs.title: Marketing & Communications Intern at The Right Place
jobs.description: Employer: The Right Place Expires: 11/29/2026 Are you a creative thinker who loves bringing ideas to life through social media, storytelling, and engaging content? Do you enjoy exploring new trends, experimenting with design, and finding creative ways to connect with audiences? Are you looking for hands-on experience where you can contribute meaningful ideas, build your skills, and see your work make an impact? If so, we want YOU to be our next Marketing & Communications Intern!About Us: Since our founding in 1985, The Right Place, Inc. (RPI) has been dedicated to driving sustainable economic growth and shared prosperity for all in the Greater Grand Rapids region. Our positive impact on the region’s economy and our tangible results in the community are only possible because of a talented, flexible, and mission-driven team.Anchored in our core values of Caring Teammates, Courageous Leaders, Can-do Attitudes, and Collaborative Doers, we’re excited to welcome a new member to our team. Every role at RPI matters—and as our Marketing & Communications Intern, you’ll have the opportunity to make a real impact and see the results of your work firsthand. Position Summary: As our Marketing & Communications Intern, you’ll play an active role on our team, supporting both our organizational marketing and Tech Week Grand Rapids. You’ll assist the team in implementing RPI’s marketing and communications strategy in support of our People, Place, and Prosperity pillars. And you’ll be involved in social media, content writing, graphic design, email marketing, event and report promotion, and web content management. You’ll gain a portfolio of published work, get a behind-the-scenes look at planning large-scale events, economic development, and mentorship from our team of professionals.The internship begins in January 2027 (application deadline Nov 30): • Spring semester (January – May): 15–20 hours per week • Possible extension into summer (May – August): 30- 35 hours per week • Possible extension into fall semester (August – December): 15–20 hours per week Key Responsibilities: • Content Creation & Social Media: Draft and build full social media campaigns for LinkedIn, Facebook, and Instagram, create graphics in Canva, and schedule approved content in Metricool. • Event & Report Promotion: Create promotion campaigns for RPI's signature events and help capture photos and live content on event day. • Tech Week Grand Rapids: Support recruitment and promotion efforts, create marketing toolkits and promotional content, coordinate with partners, and help organize event materials. • Marketing & Administrative Support: Assist with other marketing and communications projects based on team priorities. • Creative Projects: Each semester, take the lead on a self-directed creative project, such as a video or blog series, from initial concept through final production. Skills and Qualifications: • Currently enrolled in third or fourth year and pursuing a bachelor’s degree in communications, marketing, or a related field. • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to write in RPI’s brand voice and style. • Personal or professional experience using Instagram, Facebook, and LinkedIn • Proficiency in social media platforms, office software, and graphics programs. • Comfortable using AI tools to support your work. Benefits: • Holiday pay, sick time, and paid parking • Culture Team activities, professional development opportunities, and vibrant organizational culture This position works on-site in our downtown Grand Rapids office, with flexible hours between 8:30am – 5:00pm, Monday-Friday. Compensation is $17/hr. Join Our Team: We welcome you to apply for this position so that you can join us in making a positive impact on the economic health of Greater Grand Rapids and to collaborate with the best and brightest business minds.You can apply via this job posting - be sure to include your Cover Letter, Resume, and Writing Samples. You can also email the required materials to hr@rightplace.org. Links to a portfolio or social media work are encouraged.APPLICATION DEADLINE IS NOV 30.
